proof.text:
Use right-to-left composition. For consecutive arrows $h^i:A^i\to B^i$, $k^i:B^i\to C^i$ and comparisons $b_A,b_B,b_C$, the two equations $b_BT(h^0)=h^1b_A$ and $b_CT(k^0)=k^1b_B$ give
$$b_CT(k^0h^0)=b_CT(k^0)T(h^0)=k^1b_BT(h^0)=k^1h^1b_A.$$
This is just functoriality and substitution, and can be repeated for any finite string. Fix a compactification. By the local definitions in the statement, write $a_p=(\varepsilon_p\otimes1)\mu_p$ and $\pi_p=Rp_*(a_p)\eta_p$, at the displayed inputs. The hypotheses intertwine $\mu_p$, $\varepsilon_p\otimes1$, and $\eta_p$, including their input comparisons. Naturality of the supplied comparison for $Rp_*$ intertwines its application to $a_p$. Apply the displayed calculation first to $a_p$ and then to $Rp_*(a_p)\eta_p$ to obtain $b_tT(\pi_p^0)=\pi_p^1b_s$. Every intermediate object is in the supplied closed domain.

proof.text:
Expand the locally defined exchange composite. For the proper square put $Q=Lg^*Rp_*M$. The locally defined exchange is
$$e_{p,M}=Rp'_*(L\bar g'^*(\varepsilon_{p,M}))\,Rp'_*(\theta_{Rp_*M})\,\eta_{p',Q}.$$
The hypotheses give the intertwining equation for the unit at $Q$, the square comparison $\theta$, and the counit at $M$. Naturality of the supplied pullback and direct-image comparisons gives their whiskered equations at precisely these inputs. Paste these three equations using the calculation in step 1 to obtain $b_tT(e_p^0)=e_p^1b_s$. This uses neither an isomorphism assertion about $e_p$ nor a base-change theorem.

proof.text: The supplied comparison data explicitly intertwine the canonical open maps $\beta_K$ and $\gamma_{K,L}$ displayed in the statement, including the input comparisons for $K,L$. Thus their equations are $b_tT(\beta^0)=\beta^1b_s$ and $b_tT(\gamma^0)=\gamma^1b_s$. In particular $\gamma$ includes the specified pullback-composition comparison $Lj^*Lp^*\cong Lf^*$; it is not replaced by an arbitrary isomorphism of its source and target. These are hypotheses on the supplied maps; this step asserts no existence or additional property of extension by zero.

proof.text: By the local definitions in the statement, $\operatorname{PF}^c=Rp_*(\gamma)\pi_p$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=Rp'_*(\beta)e_p$, the latter evaluated at $j_!K$. Naturality of the proper direct-image comparisons gives the equations for $Rp_*(\gamma)$ and $Rp'_*(\beta)$ from step 3. Paste with steps 1 and 2 to obtain the two compactification-map equations. For whiskering by an operation $F$, naturality of $TF^0\cong F^1T$ applied to the arrow being whiskered gives the required equation; the tensor comparison is natural in both inputs, so gives it for tensoring an arrow with an identity as well. Each complete base-change route is a finite composite of these whiskered maps and the specified pullback/tensor comparisons. Apply the same two-arrow calculation to its arrows in order. Both routes therefore have the asserted comparison equation. All comparisons are natural, so these component equations hold as equations of natural transformations.

proof.text:
For a second comparison functor $S$, write $c_s,c_t$ for its comparisons at the $T$-transformed inputs. Applying $S$ to $b_tT(m^0)=m^1b_s$ and using $c_tS(m^1)=m^2c_s$ gives
$$c_tS(b_t)ST(m^0)=c_tS(m^1)S(b_s)=m^2c_sS(b_s).$$
The assumed composition cocycle identifies $c_tS(b_t)$ and $c_sS(b_s)$ with the comparisons for successive transport. The identity cocycle gives the identity case. For a compactification refinement, retain the qualification in the statement: only a supplied refinement comparison intertwining the primitive maps is considered. Insert its comparison at each intermediate object in the calculation of step 1; consecutive squares paste by that calculation, giving the refinement square for the whole composite. This does not assert unconditional compactification independence or existence of refinement compatibilities. Finally if $u^0=v^0$ are two displayed composites with common endpoints, functoriality gives $T(u^0)=T(v^0)$, and their equations give $u^1b_s=b_tT(u^0)=b_tT(v^0)=v^1b_s$. Compose with $b_s^{-1}$ to get $u^1=v^1$. This transports equality forward and uses no faithfulness, invertibility of $u,v$, or reduction of field coefficients.

title: Specified comparison functors intertwine projection and exchange composites
statement:
Fix two systems of coefficient or site categories on schemes, with pullbacks, tensor products, ordinary adjunctions and open extension maps of the types in [def-exchange-projection]. Denote the two systems by superscripts $0,1$. For each scheme $W$ let $T_W:D^0(W)\to D^1(W)$ be a comparison functor on full domains closed under the expressions below. Supply natural invertible comparisons $T_V Lu^{*,0}\cong Lu^{*,1}T_W$, $T_W Ru_*^0\cong Ru_*^1T_V$, $T_Wj_!^0\cong j_!^1T_V$, and $T_W(M\otimes^0N)\cong T_WM\otimes^1T_WN$, for every morphism $u:V\to W$ and open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow W$ being used. Require their whiskered composites to intertwine the specified units, counits, pullback square/composition maps, tensor comparisons, and canonical open maps $\beta,\gamma$. Require identity and composition cocycles for these comparisons. These are comparison data; no existence on an arbitrary domain is asserted.

Here are the precise composites meant in this assertion, with right-to-left composition and tensor symbols suppressing the coefficient system. For a compactification $c=(j,p)$, $X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, put $f=pj$. Base change along $g:Y'\to Y$, obtaining $p':\bar X'\to Y'$, $\bar g':\bar X'\to\bar X$, $j':X'\hookrightarrow\bar X'$ and $g':X'\to X$. In either system, write $\eta_u,\varepsilon_u$ for the unit and counit of $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ and supply the natural structural maps
$$\mu_{u;F,G}:Lu^*(F\otimes G)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*F\otimes Lu^*G,\qquad
\theta: Lp'^*Lg^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L\bar g'^*Lp^*.$$
For $M$ on $\bar X$ and $N$ on $Y$ set
$$a_{p;M,N}=(\varepsilon_{p,M}\otimes1)\mu_{p;Rp_*M,N},\qquad
\pi_{p;M,N}=Rp_*(a_{p;M,N})\eta_{p,Rp_*M\otimes N},$$
$$e_{p,M}=Rp'_*(L\bar g'^*\varepsilon_{p,M})\,Rp'_*(\theta_{Rp_*M})\,\eta_{p',Lg^*Rp_*M}.$$
Thus $\pi_{p;M,N}:Rp_*M\otimes N\to Rp_*(M\otimes Lp^*N)$ and $e_{p,M}:Lg^*Rp_*M\to Rp'_*L\bar g'^*M$. The canonical open maps in the hypotheses are supplied natural isomorphisms of the following types:
$$\beta_K:L\bar g'^*j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg'^*K,$$
$$\gamma_{K,N}:j_!K\otimes Lp^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(K\otimes Lj^*Lp^*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(K\otimes Lf^*N).$$
The final arrow in $\gamma$ is induced by the specified pullback-composition comparison. Put $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$, $Rf'_!^{c'}=Rp'_*j'_!$ and define
$$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,N}^c=Rp_*(\gamma_{K,N})\pi_{p;j_!K,N},\qquad
\operatorname{Ex}_!^c(K)=Rp'_*(\beta_K)e_{p,j_!K}.$$
These displayed formulas fix the meaning of the four maps locally; they assert neither existence of comparison data nor a geometric base-change or projection-formula isomorphism theorem. If $b_s:T(\operatorname{source}m^0)\cong\operatorname{source}m^1$ and $b_t:T(\operatorname{target}m^0)\cong\operatorname{target}m^1$ are the composite comparisons (including $T$ applied to the inputs), then each of the four specified maps satisfies
$$b_t\,T(m^0)=m^1\,b_s,\qquad m=\pi_p,e_p,\operatorname{PF}^c,\operatorname{Ex}_!^c.$$
The same equation holds for their whiskered composites with pullback/tensor comparisons, in particular the two complete base-change routes, as an equality of natural transformations. It respects successive comparison functors through their cocycles and compactification refinement comparisons whenever these intertwine the supplied primitive maps. Hence applying $T$ to an equality of these composites and conjugating by $b_s,b_t$ gives the corresponding equality in system 1. This assertion does not use faithfulness of $T$, invertibility of $m$, or a reduction functor on field-coefficient objects.
